title: PM chairs Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs
subtitle:
PM urges CEOs to actively participate in the next phase of India’s semiconductor growth

PM says India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies

PM reiterates  Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment

PM invites industry leaders to share suggestions on policy and administrative measures

CEOs appreciate PM’s leadership and Government’s sustained efforts to strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem

CEOs express confidence in India’s potential to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs at Seva Teerth earlier today.
During the meeting, Prime Minister emphasised the importance of close collaboration between the Government and the semiconductor industry in shaping India’s technology future. He highlighted India’s strong foundation of talent, technology adoption and infrastructure, and called for greater industry participation in skilling, innovation and emerging technologies such as AI and Quantum Computing. Referring to the target of training one crore people in AI, he said India’s talent pool, combined with the experience and capabilities of global industry leaders, can create significant opportunities.
Prime Minister said India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies. He noted the significant progress made in the semiconductor sector and said the ecosystem is now moving from foundational efforts to a phase of greater scale and opportunity.
Prime Minister reiterated the Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment, while emphasising that policies must evolve in line with technological advancements and industry requirements. He invited industry leaders to share suggestions on policy and administrative measures and assured them that their inputs would be given due consideration in further strengthening the sector. He encouraged industry leaders to actively participate in the next phase of India’s semiconductor growth.
The CEOs appreciated the Government’s sustained efforts to develop India’s semiconductor capabilities, noting the progress made in manufacturing, design, infrastructure and talent development. They expressed confidence in the opportunities emerging under ISM 2.0 and in India’s potential to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, including manufacturing, R&D, advanced technologies and supporting industries.
Appreciating the leadership and support of the Prime Minister, they said the progress achieved in recent years has created a strong foundation for further industry participation. They expressed their commitment to contributing to India’s emergence as a globally competitive semiconductor and technology hub.
The meeting was attended by CEOs, Heads and representatives of various organisations including SEMI, Micron, Infineon, Applied Materials, ASML, Merck, Tokyo Electron Ltd, FujiFilm, AMD, Intel, Tata Electronics, Lam Research, Rapidus, NXP, Foxconn, Semi Conductor Devices, Advantest, Celesta Capital, CG Power, IBM Reserach among others.

SEMICON India 2026 will feature more than 600 participating companies and is expected to attract around 50,000 visitors, with representatives from 52 countries, more than 400 executives and over 150 speakers. The exhibition will feature six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State booths, a Startup Pavilion, Innovation Showcase, Student Hackathon and Workforce Development Pavilion.

title: Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
subtitle:
Over 51 lakh additional employees expected to come under mandatory EPFO coverage

Decision strengthens formalisation and advances India’s long-term social security vision

Major step towards stronger retirement security and Viksit Bharat@2047
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month. The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers.
The EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged throughout the decade from 2004 to 2014, before being substantially enhanced to Rs.15,000 in September 2014. The present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 to reflect the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years.
At present, a fresh employee joining employment at a wage above Rs.15,000 per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework and may remain outside mandatory provident fund, pension and associated insurance protection. Raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 will bring a substantial segment of employees in the Rs.15,000– Rs.25,000 wage band within the statutory social security framework.
The approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), in accordance with the applicable scheme provisions. It will also enable the statutory contribution and pensionable-wage framework to better reflect prevailing wage levels.
Since the wage ceiling was last revised in September 2014, India has witnessed sustained wage growth, rising incomes and continued expansion of formal employment. In several States and occupations, minimum wages have also moved closer to the existing threshold. The enhancement to Rs.25,000 therefore updates the EPFO framework in line with rising wage levels and extends the benefits of formal social security to a wider segment of the workforce.
The measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection. For employers as well, wider social security coverage can support employee retention, workforce stability, morale and the development of a more secure and future-ready workforce.
The proposal underwent detailed inter-ministerial consultations and was recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 16 June 2026. The annual Government outgo is estimated at about
Rs.11,339 crore
, against the existing annual budgetary support of about
Rs.10,250 crore
. The estimated expenditure over five years is approximately
Rs.56,696 crore
.
EPFO today operates one of the world’s largest social security systems, administering the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI). The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership.
India’s workforce is at the heart of its growth story. As wages rise, incomes improve and formal employment expands, the Government’s continued emphasis on employment generation and formalisation is creating new opportunities for workers. The enhancement of the EPFO wage ceiling ensures that the social security framework also keeps pace with this progress and that a larger number of workers in formal employment receive statutory social security protection.
This approval marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture, ensuring that social protection advances alongside economic growth, rising wages and expanding formal employment as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO will undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps for implementation of the decision.

title: Third BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine Knowledge, Genetic Resources and Intellectual Property Rights Begins in Goa
subtitle: Second Meeting of BIMSTEC Nodal Group also held; Focus on Conservation, Documentation and Equitable Benefit-Sharing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 5:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Third BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine Knowledge, Genetic Resources and Intellectual Property Rights commenced today in Goa. The conference is being organised by the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, with the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), Goa, serving as the nodal institute.
The two-day conference is being held alongside the Second Meeting of the BIMSTEC Nodal Group on Traditional Medicine Knowledge, Genetic Resources and Intellectual Property Rights. Experts, officials and representatives from BIMSTEC member countries are participating in the conference.
Ms. Monalisa Das, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, and Chairperson of the Inaugural Session, highlighted the important role of the BIMSTEC Task Force for Traditional Medicine (BTFTM). She said that the Working Group can accelerate cooperation in research, education, capacity building, standardisation, pharmacopoeial development, regulatory cooperation and exchange of knowledge. She also referred to the proposed BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine, which was announced by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the Sixth BIMSTEC Summit held in Bangkok in April 2025.
In his inaugural address, Prof. Vaidya P.K. Prajapati, Director, All India Institute of Ayurveda, said that the BIMSTEC region is home to a rich and diverse heritage of traditional medicine systems, biological resources and community knowledge. He said that the conference aims to develop a collaborative framework that promotes the conservation of traditional knowledge while encouraging legitimate research and innovation, and safeguards the interests of communities through prior informed consent, mutually agreed terms and equitable benefit-sharing.
Mr. Kadirkamu Kandasamy Yoganaadan, Director – Science, Technology & Innovation and Health and Human Resource Development Division, BIMSTEC, said that the ultimate objective of regional cooperation is to improve the well-being of people, strengthen health systems and preserve the rich heritage of traditional medicine for future generations.
The technical sessions of the conference covered key issues including documentation of traditional knowledge, intellectual property rights, genetic resources, access and benefit-sharing, prior informed consent, community rights, as well as initiatives related to the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and the World Health Organization (WHO).
Representatives from BIMSTEC member countries — Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand — shared their respective national policies, legal frameworks and experiences.
The conference also discussed the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL), including controlled-access documentation, prior-art protection and the potential regional relevance of its experience.
Discussions are also focusing on artificial intelligence, documentation of traditional knowledge, intellectual property and ethical considerations.
The Second Meeting of the BIMSTEC Nodal Group will deliberate on regional cooperation, capacity building, expert networks, documentation standards, data management and potential mechanisms for collaboration. Key recommendations based on the deliberations of the conference will also be drafted to strengthen cooperation for the conservation and responsible use of traditional medicine knowledge across the BIMSTEC region.
Prof. Dr. Sujata Kadam, Dean, All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa, said that every BIMSTEC member country possesses a rich heritage of traditional knowledge developed over generations. She expressed her gratitude to all the participating delegates, experts and institutions for their contribution to the conference.
The conference will conclude on 17 September 2026.

subtitle: Committee Reviews Advanced Research, Laboratory Quality, Academic Collaboration and Infrastructure Development
date:

                16 SEP 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 6th meeting of the Institute Finance Committee (IFC) of the National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health (NHRIMH), Kottayam, was held on September 14, 2026, under the chairpersonship of Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India.
Ms. Alarmelmangai D. inaugurated the Skill Laboratory for postgraduate students at NHRIMH and visited the OPD and IPD facilities. She interacted with postgraduate students, staff and patients, and reviewed the Institute’s academic, research and patient-care activities.
The Institute Finance Committee (IFC) reviewed key areas relating to the financial, academic, research, infrastructural and administrative development of the Institute. It also reviewed the progress of decisions taken during the previous meeting and considered proposals related to institutional infrastructure, financial management, manpower requirements, academic facilities and research capabilities.
Strengthening the research ecosystem at NHRIMH was identified as a priority, with focus on expanding research programmes, upgrading laboratory infrastructure and developing facilities for advanced experimental and mechanistic research in neurological and psychiatric disorders.
The Committee also reviewed proposals for strengthening institutional capacity in line with the clinical, academic and research requirements of NHRIMH. The Committee encouraged greater collaboration with reputed national and State-level institutions through suitable MoUs to promote academic exchange, research partnerships and capacity building. The Committee also recommended organising a National Conference on World Mental Health Day.
Strengthening the quality of laboratory services was another key area of discussion. The Committee reviewed measures to enhance quality assurance mechanisms and take appropriate steps towards accreditation of laboratory facilities. Measures relating to energy efficiency, safety systems, maintenance and other essential infrastructure requirements were also considered.
The Committee stressed timely completion of approved works through effective coordination and close monitoring, with emphasis on financial prudence, quality and optimal utilisation of resources.
The meeting was attended by Dr. Preetha Kizhakkutil, Adviser (Homoeopathy), Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Subhash Kaushik, Director General, CCRH, New Delhi. The meeting was virtually attended by Dr. Srinivas Rao Chinta, Joint Adviser (Homoeopathy), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Amarendra Singh, Director, Integrated Finance Division (IFD) representative and senior officials of Ministry of Ayush.
The meeting concluded with emphasis on strengthening NHRIMH’s research, academic and clinical capabilities through improved infrastructure, quality laboratory services, institutional collaborations and timely implementation of approved initiatives.

title: On PM Modi’s Directions, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Bihar to Assess Flood Damage and Crop Loss

Bihar Flood Crisis: Centre to Extend Full Support for Relief, Crop Compensation and Rehabilitation, Says Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Patna
content:
Union Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today visited flood-affected areas of Bihar on the directions of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and took stock of the situation on the ground. Accompanied by Bihar Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, state ministers and senior officials from the Centre and the state government, Shri Chouhan conducted an extensive review of the flood situation in Hajipur, Vaishali, Munger and Bhagalpur. He travelled by motorboat, country boat and tractor to reach affected villages and agricultural fields and also conducted an aerial assessment of the situation. Interacting with flood-affected families, he assured them that the Central Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, stands firmly with the people of Bihar and will provide all possible financial and infrastructure support to help the state overcome the crisis.

Government

The Centre is closely monitoring the flood situation in Bihar following a sharp and, in several areas, record rise in the water levels of the Ganga and other rivers. On the Prime Minister’s directions, Shri Chouhan reached Bihar on Tuesday along with a high-level central team comprising senior officials and technical experts from the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development and various central institutions. After reaching Patna, he began the field assessment along with Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, members of the state Cabinet and senior administrative officials.

Visits

Villages
Fields
and
Relief
Camps
In Hajipur, Vaishali, Shri Chouhan visited the worst-affected villages of Terasia and Saraipur, where he travelled by motorboat and country boat to inspect inundated residential areas and agricultural fields. At several difficult-to-reach locations, he travelled by tractor to assess the situation. He also reviewed the extent of flooding and water levels from the Raghopur Six-Lane Bridge. In Munger, the Union Minister inspected the Nawagarhi relief camp and the Kojikaraiya embankment and reviewed arrangements for safety and water drainage. In Bhagalpur, he visited relief camps and interacted with flood-affected people who had taken shelter there.

Floods
After the field visits, Shri Chouhan told the media that, according to information shared by the Chief Minister and local residents, water levels in the affected areas have risen nearly one foot above the levels recorded during the historic floods of 2016. He said banana and maize crops have been severely damaged after remaining submerged for more than 10 days. Nearly 50 lakh people have been directly affected by the floods. Many families have been forced to leave their homes, houses have been damaged and livestock has also been lost. “Seeing farmers’ crops, on which they have invested their hard work and livelihood, submerged in floodwater is deeply painful. But farmers need not lose heart. The government is fully committed to protecting their livelihoods and supporting them through this difficult time,” Shri Chouhan said.

Government’s
Relief
and
Rescue
Efforts
Reviewed
Shri Chouhan appreciated the state government’s response to the situation and said that the administration, under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, is working round the clock on relief and rescue operations. As part of immediate assistance, the state government has begun transferring Rs 7,000 directly into the bank accounts of each affected family through DBT. The process is being carried out on a war footing. Doctors and paramedical teams are being sent by boat to flood-affected areas to provide medical assistance and medicines to people in their homes and at relief camps. Arrangements have also been made for safe shelter, clean drinking water, dry rations and cooked food packets for affected families.

Assessment
Shri Chouhan said that while the state government is providing immediate assistance through its State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and available resources, the Central Government will extend all necessary support for relief, recovery and reconstruction. Officials from the Agriculture and Rural Development departments are conducting a preliminary assessment of the situation. A detailed Inter-Ministerial Central Team will subsequently be sent to Bihar to assess the extent of damage. The team will assess losses across affected districts, particularly damage to agricultural crops, roads, bridges, houses and livestock. Shri Chouhan said that once the state government submits the required proposal under the National Disaster Response Fund, the Centre will provide adequate financial and material assistance without delay.

Reassuring flood-affected families, Shri Chouhan said that the Centre and the Prime Minister stand firmly with the people of Bihar. “I assure the people of Bihar, on behalf of the Central Government and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, that although the crisis is serious, our resolve to serve the people is stronger. We will stand shoulder to shoulder with the state government in helping Bihar overcome this crisis. No affected family will be left helpless,” he said.

at

After the day-long visit to flood-affected areas, embankments and relief camps across the state, Shri Chouhan will chair a high-level review meeting at 6 PM today at the Chief Minister’s residence on Anne Marg. Senior officials from the concerned departments of the Central and state governments will attend the meeting. The review will cover the distribution of relief material, healthcare services, the plan for crop compensation and restoration of damaged infrastructure. Necessary directions will be issued accordingly.

title: Government Eases RCMC Requirement for Export Consignments up to ₹3 Lakh
subtitle: RCMC Exemption Lowers Entry Barriers for MSMEs and First-Time Exporters
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 2:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government has introduced a de minimis exemption from the requirement of Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) or Certificate of Registration for small-value export consignments up to ₹3 lakh. The measure is aimed at reducing the compliance burden for new and small exporters and facilitating exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels.
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has amended Para 2.57 of the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023 to provide that RCMC or Certificate of Registration will not be required for export consignments having a Free-on-Board (FOB) value of up to ₹3 lakh, wherever such certificate is otherwise required under the Foreign Trade Policy. Export consignments exceeding ₹3 lakh will continue to require a valid RCMC or Certificate of Registration, wherever applicable.
Historical data for the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26) indicates that low-value exports account for a significant share of shipping bills but a very small proportion of the overall export value. Consignments up to USD 3,000, for instance, account for 43 per cent of shipping bills but only 0.86 per cent of India’s total merchandise export value. The exemption is therefore expected to cover a substantial number of small-value export transactions while having only a marginal impact on the overall value of exports.
At present, exporters are generally required to obtain an RCMC or Certificate of Registration from the relevant Export Promotion Council or Commodity Board, wherever applicable under the Foreign Trade Policy. For new or occasional exporters undertaking small-value consignments, this involves an additional compliance step, including identifying the appropriate registering body, submitting the prescribed documents and completing the registration process before undertaking exports.
The measure provides MSMEs, artisans, small businesses and first-time exporters with a simpler entry point into international markets by removing the requirement to obtain an RCMC upfront for eligible small-value consignments. This will enable emerging exporters to test overseas markets and establish an export track record with lower initial compliance requirements.
As exporters expand their operations and their consignments move beyond the ₹3 lakh threshold, they can obtain membership of the relevant Export Promotion Councils or Commodity Boards and access export promotion, market access and other institutional support services.
The measure offers lower entry barriers for new exporters, enabling first-time and occasional exporters to undertake eligible small-value exports without obtaining an RCMC upfront. It is particularly beneficial for MSMEs and small businesses, as small manufacturers, artisans, entrepreneurs and emerging exporters will be able to explore overseas markets and build an export track record with lower initial compliance requirements.
The exemption will also facilitate e-commerce and other emerging export channels. It is expected to support low-value exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels that are increasingly enabling businesses to reach international customers.
The measure will support the gradual integration of emerging exporters into global markets. As exporters scale up and undertake higher-value consignments, they can obtain RCMC membership and access the wider range of export promotion and institutional support provided through Export Promotion Councils and other prescribed bodies.
At the same time, the existing framework for larger exports remains unchanged. The exemption is limited to small-value consignments, while the requirement of RCMC or Certificate of Registration will continue for consignments exceeding ₹3 lakh, wherever otherwise applicable.
The measure will also help broaden the base of Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Boards by encouraging greater participation of MSMEs in exports. By lowering the initial compliance barrier, more MSMEs will be able to enter international markets and, as their export operations scale beyond the ₹3 lakh threshold, obtain RCMC and become members of the relevant EPCs or Commodity Boards to access export promotion activities, market access initiatives and other institutional support.
The measure reinforces the Government’s commitment to reducing the compliance burden, broadening participation in exports and making international trade more accessible to MSMEs, first-time exporters and emerging businesses.

An accompanying exhibition will provide visitors an opportunity to view the mementos and appreciate their artistic and cultural significance before participating in the e-auction. The exhibition will also enable the public to explore the diversity of India’s traditional crafts, artistic practices and cultural expressions represented in the collection.
The Ministry of Culture invites citizens, collectors, institutions, corporates, art enthusiasts and members of the public from India to explore the collection, visit the exhibition and participate in the 8th Edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction.
The PM Mementos e-Auction is an initiative that celebrates India’s heritage, art, craftsmanship and cultural diversity, while enabling public participation and contributing towards a significant national cause through the Namami Gange Programme.

title: CAQM conducts special inspection of industries in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh; 16 of 22 units inspected found non-compliant, 12 Show Cause Notices issued
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:

                16 SEP 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a special inspection of industries operating in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh, on 15.09.2026, during which 22 industrial units were inspected, 16 were found non-compliant with applicable norms and Statutory Directions and 12 Show Cause Notices (SCNs) were issued.
The inspection drive was carried out by 7 Flying Squads of CAQM in coordination with the District Administration and concerned authorities. The inspections covered industrial areas of Masuri-Gulawati Road, Pilkhuwa, Ravali/Shekhpur/M.G. Road, Tatarpur/Garh Road, Railway Road/Textile Centre Road and Ravala/Shekhar. Of the 22 units inspected, 6 were found compliant, while 16 were found non-compliant with the applicable norms and Statutory Directions.
Various instances of non-compliance were observed during the inspections, including intense visible smoke, inadequate Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), non-installation or improper functioning of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS), bypass arrangements in wet scrubber systems and leakages in APCD/wet scrubber systems. Non-compliance of DG sets with statutory
directions, discrepancies in Consent to Operate (CTO) and DG set capacity/fuel details, non-availability of stack emission reports and stacks not conforming to Emission Regulation Part-III (ERP-III) guidelines were also observed.
During the inspection drive, entry was denied by two suspected illegal units. Accordingly, strict action/re-inspections have been proposed. Instances of illegal/non-conforming industrial units, use of a wood-fired pit furnace with hazardous sludge, and non-installation of stack monitoring/Retrofitted Emission Control Device (RECD) systems were also observed. One unit using a wood-fired pit furnace with hazardous sludge and another non-conforming unit were sealed by the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB).
The inspection teams also identified industrial units operating in compliance with the applicable norms. The findings of the inspection teams have been documented for further necessary action by the concerned authorities.
Based on the observations made during the inspection drive, 12 Show Cause Notices (SCNs) have been issued to the concerned units. CAQM has reiterated that all industrial units are required to strictly comply with applicable environmental norms, Statutory Directions, CTO conditions and other prescribed measures. Any instance of non-compliance shall be dealt with in accordance with applicable environmental laws and regulations. The concerned authorities have been advised to take necessary action(s) to ensure compliance.
CAQM continues to undertake special inspection drives across NCR to identify instances of non-compliance, strengthen enforcement and ensure effective implementation of Statutory Directions by industries and other pollution-generating sectors.

title: India reaffirms Commitment to Ozone Layer Protection and Climate Action at 32nd World Ozone Day Celebration in Mumbai
subtitle:
The Country has exceeded its Montreal Protocol commitments without compromising Development: MoS (EFCC) Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh

Maharashtra working towards Prime Minister's vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 through Sustainable Development: State Environment Minister Smt. Pankaja Munde

India’s Net Zero Portal and NAPCC Dashboard launched on World Ozone Day 2026

248 ITIs adopted by 12 Refrigeration and Airconditioning (RAC) Manufacturers; To align Training of next generation of Technicians with Industry Standards
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 3:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change today organised the national celebration of the 32nd World Ozone Day in Mumbai, with the theme
‘Global Action for a Cooler Planet’.
The event was presided over by Union Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Maharashtra State Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Smt. Pankaja Munde.
The event was also graced by the presence of Secretary (EFCC), Shri Tanmay Kumar; Ms. Angela Lusigi, Country Head (UNDP); Ms. Ulrike Ebeling, Country Director and Head (GIZ India), besides senior officials from Governments of India and Maharashtra, besides representatives of international organisations, industry representatives, academic experts and school children to highlight India’s efforts towards protection of the ozone layer and a cooler and more sustainable planet.
On the occasion, the dignitaries launched India's Net Zero Portal and the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) Dashboard. The Net Zero portal will serve as a central repository to track, coordinate and showcase India’s climate commitments and enable industries, organisations and government bodies to voluntarily register and display their progress towards net-zero emissions. Further, the NAPCC Portal was also launched as a centralised digital gateway showcasing India’s overarching National Action Plan on Climate Change, with tracking and insights across national missions.
(Press Release:
https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2310737&reg=48&lang=2
)
Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh said India has demonstrated that economic growth and environmental protection can go hand in hand. The Minister said India has shown proactive leadership in conservation and has met its commitments under the Montreal Protocol without compromising development. He emphasised that collective action involving governments, scientists, industry, officers and citizens is essential to address environmental challenges.
Shri Singh highlighted Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) as a framework for translating environmental protection into simple, everyday actions. The Minister said mindful utilisation of natural resources, instead of wasteful consumption, can enable citizens to contribute to environmental conservation. He urged citizens to adopt three measures for sustainable cooling: get air-conditioners serviced by certified and skilled technicians who handle refrigerants safely; set AC temperatures at a comfortable level, preferably around 24 degrees Celsius, to save electricity and reduce carbon emissions; and choose high star-rated, energy-efficient appliances using climate-friendly refrigerants.
Smt. Munde said Maharashtra is working towards Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision for a developed India by 2047, with a focus on decarbonisation, sustainable development and environment-friendly growth. She said Maharashtra is preparing roadmaps and action plans to integrate ozone-layer protection and climate action, while also advancing energy-efficient and climate-responsive cooling systems and buildings, particularly in view of the State’s rapid urbanisation and rising temperatures.
UNDP Country Head Ms. Angela Lusigi said India’s implementation of the Montreal Protocol demonstrates that economic growth and environmental protection can advance together. Highlighting India’s progress in phasing out ozone-depleting substances, she said the country’s targets have often been achieved ahead of schedule, while promoting low-impact technologies, strengthening small and medium enterprises and training technicians in new refrigerants, creating opportunities for green jobs.
GIZ Country Director and Head Ms. Ulrike Ebeling said that India and Germany are working together to advance climate-friendly cooling solutions and support implementation of the HCFC Phase-out Management Plan Stage III (2025–2030), with a focus on the refrigeration and air-conditioning servicing sector. She highlighted efforts to establish a nationally recognised certification system for air-conditioning technicians, with a target to train 25,000 technicians by 2030, besides strengthening training capacity in the cooling sector.
The event also witnessed the announcement of the adoption of 248 Industrial Training Institutions by 12 Refrigeration and Airconditioning (RAC) manufacturers through a 4-Party Memorandum of Agreement comprising RAC manufacturers, Ozone Cell, Regional Directorate, Directorate General of Training (DGT) and State Directorate, DGT. The initiative is aimed at strengthening training infrastructure for the next generation of technicians. The institutional partnership aims to align classroom learning with industry standards. This synergy will build a workforce skilled in eco-friendly, low-global-warming-potential (GWP) technologies, directly supporting India’s commitments under the Montreal Protocol and the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP).
Publications based on studies conducted by the Ozone Cell, MoEF&CC were released on the occasion. The event also featured the announcement of winners of a national school-level poster and slogan writing competitions, as well as winners of a national online quiz competition. A video film showcasing India’s proactive industrial transformation and pioneering strides towards a cooler, more sustainable planet was also screened.
India has been a Party to the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer and the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer and all its amendments since 1992. The country has met all its commitments under the Montreal Protocol schedule for different ozone-depleting substances. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), Carbon tetrachloride (CTC) and Halons have already been phased out for controlled applications, while India is currently phasing out Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) as per the accelerated phase-out schedule of the Montreal Protocol. India has already met the 2015, 2020 and 2025 phase-out targets for HCFCs.
India ratified the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol in September 2021. The Kigali Amendment came into force for India on 26 December 2021. As per the agreed phase-down schedule, India will complete the phase-down of HFC production and consumption in four steps from 2032 onwards, with reductions of 10 per cent in 2032, 20 per cent in 2037, 30 per cent in 2042 and 85 per cent in 2047, against the baseline.

The
Net Zero Portal
is a centralised digital platform for voluntary registration and disclosure of Net Zero commitments by Indian entities across sectors. Participating entities can disclose their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, declare Net Zero targets and provide annual progress updates. Entities are encouraged to report Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while reporting of Scope 3 emissions remains voluntary. The Portal also enables entities to outline pathways towards Net Zero, including measures related to clean energy transition, energy efficiency, technological interventions and carbon removals, as applicable.
The initiative brings voluntary climate actions onto a common platform, enhances transparency and encourages credible long-term climate planning. Entities successfully declaring their Net Zero targets will receive an acknowledgement from the MoEFCC. https://netzeroindia.moef.gov.in/

provides a consolidated digital view of implementation and progress across the National Missions under the NAPCC. The Dashboard will strengthen inter-ministerial coordination, support evidence-based assessment of national climate actions, help assess sectoral progress, identify implementation gaps and consolidate relevant inputs from Ministries and Departments. It is also expected to strengthen the linkages between domestic climate actions and India’s international climate commitments. The Dashboard can be accessed at:
https://napccindia.moef.gov.in/

title: CBIC commemorates 10 years of India’s Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) Programme; Outlines way forward and reaffirms commitment to trusted trade
subtitle:
AEO Programme is pivotal in transforming India’s customs administration into a modern, trusted and facilitative system aligned with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards: CBIC Chairman


CBIC Member (Customs) noted transformation of Customs from a transaction-centric approach to a risk-based and trust-oriented model of administration since the introduction of the current AEO framework
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 3:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) today celebrated a decade of India’s Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) Programme with a commemorative event titled “AEO@10: Accelerating Growth, Enhancing Trust, Optimizing Trade” in New Delhi.
The event brought together policymakers, industry leaders, logistics stakeholders, WCO experts and Authorised Economic Operators to reflect on the programme’s achievements and chart the roadmap for its future.
Addressing the gathering as Chief Guest, Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, underscored the pivotal role played by the AEO Programme in transforming India’s customs administration into a modern, trusted and facilitative system aligned with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards.
He noted that the programme has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s trade facilitation architecture by promoting voluntary compliance, strengthening supply chain security and enabling faster, more predictable cross-border movement of goods. The CBIC Chairman outlined five big ideas for the next decade:
technology-driven facilitation
radical inclusivity for MSMEs
seamless inter-agency coordination
global leadership through expanded Mutual Recognition Arrangements, and
synergy across indirect tax verticals
Highlighting CBIC’s commitment to stakeholder-centric reforms, the Chairman announced the launch of a structured feedback response form on the AEO portal to enable continuous and systematic inputs from AEO entities and other stakeholders.
Drawing on Pillar 2 of the WCO SAFE Framework and the CBIC Citizens’ Charter, he emphasised that trade is an equal partner in building a trusted ecosystem and that feedback must be continuous. He also referred to the Eligible Manufacturer Importer (EMI) Scheme, highlighted by the Union Finance Minister’s in the Union Budget speech, as an important stepping stone that rewards early compliance and creates a natural pathway to higher AEO tiers.
In his address, Member (Customs), CBIC, recalled the transformation of Customs from a transaction-centric approach to a risk-based and trust-oriented model of administration since the introduction of the current AEO framework through Circular No. 33/2016-Customs. He underlined that voluntary compliance promotes good governance, reduces supply-chain risk and transaction costs, and that supply-chain security remains central to the resilience of India’s trade ecosystem. He noted that important discussions at the annual Customs Consultative Group meeting held in Kolkata, together with representations from trade, have informed several trade-friendly process improvements now under consideration. These include a unified Standard Operating Procedure for uniform processing across zones; a clear checklist for applicants and Zonal AEO Programme Managers; a single-deficiency approach; time-bound processing; copying of deficiency communications to the applicant; a clarified position on financial solvency; and strengthening of dedicated Client Relationship Managers and trained validators, in line with the National Trade Facilitation Action Plan.
The Member (Customs) also stated that, in the same spirit of reducing compliance burden, documentation requirements under the EMI Scheme have already been rationalised through Circular No. 39/2026-Customs dated 3rd September 2026, bringing down the documents to be uploaded from ten to three, with effect from 15th September 2026.
The event marked the launch of the commemorative publication “A Decade of AEO in India: Celebrating Trusted Trade Partnerships”, documenting the evolution, milestones and impact of India’s AEO Programme over the past ten years, and incorporating contributions from CBIC officers, international partners, trade and industry. A stakeholder feedback survey on the AEO Programme was also announced to obtain structured inputs from industry for guiding future reforms. In addition, new AEO certificates were presented to select businesses, recognising their commitment to secure and compliant international trade.
In her welcome address earlier, Dr. Kavita Bhatnagar, Principal Commissioner and National AEO Programme Manager, highlighted the remarkable growth of the programme since its inception and emphasised the importance of continued collaboration between Customs and the trade community in building a trusted and resilient trading environment.
Representatives from leading industry bodies, including the Federation of Freight Forwarders’ Associations in India (FFFAI), appreciated the significant contribution of the AEO Programme towards improving ease of doing business, reducing transaction costs and enhancing supply chain predictability. Leading AEO entities also shared their experiences, highlighting tangible benefits such as expedited customs clearance, improved operational efficiency and strengthened global business confidence.
India’s AEO Programme has, over the past decade, become an important pillar of CBIC’s trade facilitation initiatives by rewarding compliant businesses with simplified customs procedures and risk-based facilitation while maintaining robust supply chain security.
As of date, 5,967 entities — comprising importers, exporters, manufacturers, customs brokers, logistics operators and warehouse operators — have been certified under the AEO Programme across T1, T2, T3 and LO categories
.
The programme has steadily expanded its coverage of the logistics chain, digitised application processes, established dedicated AEO Cells, and introduced special facilitative provisions for MSMEs. As India continues to expand its engagement with trusted trading partners across the world, CBIC remains committed to further strengthening the AEO Programme through stakeholder-centric reforms, technology adoption, international cooperation and continuous feedback from trade, thereby contributing to the objectives of Viksit Bharat @2047 and making India an increasingly preferred destination for global trade and investment.

title: Department of Fisheries to Organize National Workshop on Promotion of Deep-Sea Fishing and Interaction with Access Pass and LoA Holders
subtitle: Major Focus on Technology, Financing, Skill development and Market Linkages promoting Harnessing of High-Value Marine Resources and Seafood Exports
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:

content:
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is organizing a
National Workshop on Promotion of Deep-Sea Fishing and Interaction with Access Pass and LoA Holders
on
17th September 2026
in
Gandhinagar, Gujarat
. The National workshop aims to promote deep-sea fishing by encouraging fishers to harness high-value fisheries resources, while also providing a platform to understand on-ground challenges and gather stakeholder suggestions for further strengthening the sector.
The National workshop will be graced by presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Gujarat, along with Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj. The event will also witness the participation of fishers including women fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Gujarat and all other coastal States/UTs, ICAR, CIFNET, NABARD, NCEL, NCDC, SEAI, MPEDA, EIC and other fisheries stakeholders.
Department of Fisheries, Government of India has given special thrust to strengthening fisheries farmer producer organizations (FFPO) and fisheries cooperatives while also focusing on digitization of the fisheries sector through various initiatives.
The National workshop will feature focused technical sessions covering the entire deep-sea fishing value chain, from resource potential and vessel modernization to skill development, financing, processing, value addition and access to export markets. Discussions will explore opportunities for harnessing high-value fisheries resources in India’s EEZ and High Seas, adoption of modern fishing technologies and global best practices, capacity building for fishers and crew, access to institutional finance and cooperative-led investment models, and strengthening of post-harvest management, traceability, value addition, and export compliance systems. Each session will comprise expert presentations, fishers or industry perspectives, and stakeholder discussions, providing participants with practical insights and a comprehensive understanding of the opportunities, challenges, and support mechanisms available for advancing deep-sea fishing in India.
The deliberations are expected to serve as a significant platform for strengthening India’s deep-sea fishing ecosystem by bringing together policymakers, technical experts, financial institutions, industry stakeholders, cooperatives, and fishers for focused deliberations. The discussions and recommendations emerging from the workshop will help identify practical solutions to on-ground challenges, improve access to technology, skills, finance, and markets, and facilitate greater participation of fishers in deep-sea fishing.
Background
India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of about 24 lakh sq. km. The marine fisheries potential within India’s EEZ is estimated at 58.6 lakh MT, supporting the livelihoods of approximately 50 lakh fishers and contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export revenues. India is presently among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing countries globally and exported seafood valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26.
Most fishing activities are concentrated within 40–50 nautical miles of the coast, while deeper waters and areas beyond national jurisdiction offer substantial opportunities for harvesting high-value species, particularly tuna and tuna-like resources. recognising the strategic importance of sustainable marine fisheries, the Government of India, has notified enabling framework including Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025 and High Seas Guidelines, 2025 for sustainable harnessing of fisheries resources by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels.
The Access Pass for fishing in India's EEZ, is a free digital pass issued via the
ReALCRaft
Portal. Its core objective is to empower the traditional fishers, cooperatives, and Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) for fishing in the EEZ (12 to 200 nautical miles), while ensuring sustainability of oceanic fishery resources. The Access Pass is issued under the
Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Rules, 2025
notified by the Government of India on 04 November 2025. The Access Pass is required for mechanized fishing vessels and large motorized boats over 24 meters length, while traditional non-motorized and small artisanal crafts are fully exempted to protect local livelihoods. This landmark initiative aims to empower traditional and small-scale fishermen, Fisheries Cooperative Societies, and Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to expand fishing operations, harness untapped resources through deep-sea fishing, and access new income streams through processing and exports, thereby enhancing livelihoods. As per the EEZ Rules, the Access Pass is required for undertaking fishing operations in the EEZ of India, beyond 12 nautical miles. So far, a total of 9,650 Access Passes have been issued based on applications received through coastal States and Union Territories.

title: Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
subtitle:
Union Ministers Shri C. R. Paatil, Shri Tokhan Sahu and Shri V. Somanna call for nationwide participation in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

SHS 2026 campaign places students and youth at the heart of sustained behaviour change for Swachhata

‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’ announced as the theme of SHS 2026
date:
Posted On:
                16 SEP 2026 9:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu addressed a curtain-raiser media interaction for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 at the National Media Centre in New Delhi today.
Observed annually since 2017, Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, beginning from 17th September this year, brings citizens, institutions and leadership together to strengthen voluntarism and collective action for Swachhata. The SHS 2026 theme, ‘
Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’
, underlines that Swachhata is a shared responsibility and that the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat can be realized only through the active participation of all citizens.
The national curtain-raiser event/ interaction was held ahead of the nationwide campaign beginning tomorrow. Jointly organized by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Department of Urban Development (DoUD) Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, SHS 2026 will bring together Central Ministries and Departments, States/UTs Rural and Urban local bodies, institutions and other stakeholders for collective action for Swachhata.
Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, underscored that, under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Swachhata has evolved into a national movement driven by Jan Bhagidari. He noted that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has consistently led this movement from the front and inspired citizens across the country. Emphasizing that cleanliness is a shared responsibility, he called upon every citizen, particularly students and youth, to participate wholeheartedly in SHS 2026 and strengthen the collective resolve for a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat. The Minister cited the example of Navsari’s ‘Swachhata Se Swagat’- Micro Swachhata Abhiyaan before the visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister, where people from all walks of life came together for micro cleaning in villages. He also referred to the example of Surat for prompt cleaning after Visarjan of Ganpati last year and people coming together for support, recognition and felicitation of sanitation workers. He mentioned that people are now increasingly coming out to participate and contribute to Swachhata which is the awareness and behaviour change brought about by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in the country.
In a virtual message, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, called upon States to ensure enthusiastic participation in the upcoming
Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
campaign. He requested that citizens begin the campaign by cleaning their own homes on 17th September. He further requested that all Ministers, MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners and eminent personalities of the State should participate in Nation-wide shramdaan on 1st October. He also urged that cleanliness activities at public places be organized on 2nd October, or Swachh Bharat Diwas, in remembrance of Mahatma Gandhi. He also appealed to students and youth, sportspersons, artists, spiritual leaders, and other Swachhata ambassadors to use their platforms to encourage wider public participation and collective action at the grassroots.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu said, “The message of swachhata will be effective only when our government offices and institutions themselves set the example. All departments must ensure visible cleanliness in their offices, premises, and subordinate units, along with citizen mobilization, so that this campaign becomes a powerful demonstration of participation —a ‘Whole of Government’ and a ‘Whole of Society’ approach. Every Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat, every ward, every institution, every community, must be connected with this campaign, making cleanliness a shared national resolve.”
The Secretaries of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation and the Department of Urban Development highlighted the campaign framework.
The five key pillars of SHS 2026 are:
Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places:
Identification, mapping and time-bound transformation of difficult and dirty spots, along with cleanliness drives at CTUs and high-footfall public places.
Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata:
Engagement of students and youth through
‘Swachhata Gyan Yatra’
exposure visits to solid waste management facilities and
‘Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad’
covering Swachhata, rainwater harvesting and water management.
SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir:
Single-window camps facilitating health check-ups, PPE and safety gear, and linkages with eligible Central and State welfare schemes. Safai Mitras, Swachhagrahis and sanitation workers will also be felicitated locally in recognition of their contribution for Swachhata.
Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata:
Citizen engagement, awareness on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and 4-way source segregation and composting. Activities will also include
Sports for Swachhata
;
Swachh Parv, Harit Parv
; plantation drives under ‘
Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’
; World Tourism Day activities (27thSeptember, 2026); and
Special Gram Sabhas
and
Council Meetings
on Swachh Bharat Diwas (2ndOctober, 2026)
.
Swachhata se Samriddhi:
Promotion of circularity through
‘
Waste to Wealth’, and
Waste to Art’; donation and RRR initiatives for old books, toys and clothes, and Plastic Recycling Melas involving Bulk Waste Generators.
Recognizing children and youth as change-makers and the future custodians of Swachh Bharat, SHS 2026 envisages their active involvement through
Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata
in building sustained habits for cleanliness, Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and four-way source segregation. Initiatives like
Sports for Swachhata
envisages using local and regional sports to engage children, youth and communities for carrying Swachhata into schools, institutions, cities and villages.
A simultaneous nationwide
shramdaan
, ‘
Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath
’, will be organized on 1st October 2026 from 8-9 AM. This will have citizens from different walks of life come together to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service.
On 2nd October 2026, observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas,
Special Gram Sabhas
will be organized in rural areas, and
Special Council Meetings
will be organized in urban areas. The Special Gram Sabhas will, among other aspects, focus on outcomes of SHS 2026 and awareness on SWM Rules, 2026. The
Swachh Seva Aankalan
launched by DDWS for rural areas on 15th September 2026 will also be discussed during the Special Gram Sabhas.  Both cities and villages will conduct plantation drives on this day under ‘
Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam
’
. On this day Swachhata Pledge will also be voluntarily taken by citizens across the country through MyGov platform.
The SHS 2026 theme, logo, campaign brochure and portal were launched during the event along with
SHS 2026 anthem
. A curtain raiser video on SHS 2026 was also shown.
Through widespread Jan Bhagidari, SHS 2026 seeks to reinforce Swachhata as a shared responsibility and translate citizen participation into sustained action towards a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Citizens and participating organizations are encouraged to undertake and share their activities using the hashtags #SHS2026 and #SwachhataHiSeva2026.

Observed annually since 2017, Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, beginning from 17th September this year, brings citizens, institutions and leadership together to strengthen voluntarism and collective action for Swachhata. The SHS 2026 theme, ‘
Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’
, underlines that Swachhata is a shared responsibility and that the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat can be realized only through the active participation of all citizens.
The national curtain-raiser event/ interaction was held ahead of the nationwide campaign beginning tomorrow. Jointly organized by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Department of Urban Development (DoUD) Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, SHS 2026 will bring together Central Ministries and Departments, States/UTs Rural and Urban local bodies, institutions and other stakeholders for collective action for Swachhata.
Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, underscored that, under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Swachhata has evolved into a national movement driven by Jan Bhagidari. He noted that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has consistently led this movement from the front and inspired citizens across the country. Emphasizing that cleanliness is a shared responsibility, he called upon every citizen, particularly students and youth, to participate wholeheartedly in SHS 2026 and strengthen the collective resolve for a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat. The Minister cited the example of Navsari’s ‘Swachhata Se Swagat’- Micro Swachhata Abhiyaan before the visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister, where people from all walks of life came together for micro cleaning in villages. He also referred to the example of Surat for prompt cleaning after Visarjan of Ganpati last year and people coming together for support, recognition and felicitation of sanitation workers. He mentioned that people are now increasingly coming out to participate and contribute to Swachhata which is the awareness and behaviour change brought about by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in the country.
In a virtual message, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, called upon States to ensure enthusiastic participation in the upcoming
Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
campaign. He requested that citizens begin the campaign by cleaning their own homes on 17th September. He further requested that all Ministers, MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners and eminent personalities of the State should participate in Nation-wide shramdaan on 1st October. He also urged that cleanliness activities at public places be organized on 2nd October, or Swachh Bharat Diwas, in remembrance of Mahatma Gandhi. He also appealed to students and youth, sportspersons, artists, spiritual leaders, and other Swachhata ambassadors to use their platforms to encourage wider public participation and collective action at the grassroots.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu said, “The message of swachhata will be effective only when our government offices and institutions themselves set the example. All departments must ensure visible cleanliness in their offices, premises, and subordinate units, along with citizen mobilization, so that this campaign becomes a powerful demonstration of participation —a ‘Whole of Government’ and a ‘Whole of Society’ approach. Every Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat, every ward, every institution, every community, must be connected with this campaign, making cleanliness a shared national resolve.”
The Secretaries of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation and the Department of Urban Development highlighted the campaign framework.
The five key pillars of SHS 2026 are:
Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places:
Identification, mapping and time-bound transformation of difficult and dirty spots, along with cleanliness drives at CTUs and high-footfall public places.
Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata:
Engagement of students and youth through
‘Swachhata Gyan Yatra’
exposure visits to solid waste management facilities and
‘Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad’
covering Swachhata, rainwater harvesting and water management.
SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir:
Single-window camps facilitating health check-ups, PPE and safety gear, and linkages with eligible Central and State welfare schemes. Safai Mitras, Swachhagrahis and sanitation workers will also be felicitated locally in recognition of their contribution for Swachhata.
Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata:
Citizen engagement, awareness on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and 4-way source segregation and composting. Activities will also include
Sports for Swachhata
;
Swachh Parv, Harit Parv
; plantation drives under ‘
Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’
; World Tourism Day activities (27thSeptember, 2026); and
Special Gram Sabhas
and
Council Meetings
on Swachh Bharat Diwas (2ndOctober, 2026)
.
Swachhata se Samriddhi:
Promotion of circularity through
‘
Waste to Wealth’, and
Waste to Art’; donation and RRR initiatives for old books, toys and clothes, and Plastic Recycling Melas involving Bulk Waste Generators.
Recognizing children and youth as change-makers and the future custodians of Swachh Bharat, SHS 2026 envisages their active involvement through
Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata
in building sustained habits for cleanliness, Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and four-way source segregation. Initiatives like
Sports for Swachhata
envisages using local and regional sports to engage children, youth and communities for carrying Swachhata into schools, institutions, cities and villages.
A simultaneous nationwide
shramdaan
, ‘
Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath
’, will be organized on 1st October 2026 from 8-9 AM. This will have citizens from different walks of life come together to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service.
On 2nd October 2026, observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas,
Special Gram Sabhas
will be organized in rural areas, and
Special Council Meetings
will be organized in urban areas. The Special Gram Sabhas will, among other aspects, focus on outcomes of SHS 2026 and awareness on SWM Rules, 2026. The
Swachh Seva Aankalan
launched by DDWS for rural areas on 15th September 2026 will also be discussed during the Special Gram Sabhas.  Both cities and villages will conduct plantation drives on this day under ‘
Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam
’

The SHS 2026 theme, logo, campaign brochure and portal were launched during the event along with
SHS 2026 anthem
. A curtain raiser video on SHS 2026 was also shown.
Through widespread Jan Bhagidari, SHS 2026 seeks to reinforce Swachhata as a shared responsibility and translate citizen participation into sustained action towards a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Citizens and participating organizations are encouraged to undertake and share their activities using the hashtags #SHS2026 and #SwachhataHiSeva2026.

title: Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation launches Swachh Seva Aankalan for Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen)
subtitle:

Gram Sabha validation to strengthen community participation, transparency and accountability
date:

                16 SEP 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil launched Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) on 15th September 2026 during a virtual meeting with States/UTs. The meeting was attended by the Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna.  Ministers in charge of Rural Sanitation and concerned officials and Mission Directors of Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) from States/UTs joined virtually.
Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) is an annual, Gram Panchayat level digital self-assessment framework developed by Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) 2.0 for assessment and monitoring of sanitation service delivery in rural areas. This multi-tier evaluation framework envisages the involvement of Gram Panchayats, Gram Sabhas, Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSC), District and State/UT level officials for strengthening sanitation service delivery at grass root level.
Under SSA, ODF Plus (Model) declared Gram Panchayats, together with their VWSCs and local communities, will assess the status of ODF sustainability, visual cleanliness and Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) in the Gram Panchayat. The functionality and Operation & Maintenance (O&M) status of sanitation and community SLWM assets will also be self-assessed through the Aankalan. The findings will be discussed and validated by the concerned Gram Sabha and will be available to the District and State/UT authorities to be reviewed in DWSM/SWSM meetings. These authorities will be able to identify service delivery gaps and prepare their respective improvement plans for corrective action at grassroot level.
In the spirit of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, this will further empower the Gram Panchayats and Gram Sabhas to review their achievements and progress and make focused efforts for improvement in the same.

mployees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has been enhanced from Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 25,000 per month with effect from Vishwakarma Jayanti and Sewa Divas on 17 September 2026. Addressing the media, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said that the enhancement of the statutory wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month marks an important step towards strengthening social security for workers. The revised ceiling, which will come into effect from 17 September 2026 on the occasion of Vishwakarma Jayanti and Sewa Divas, will enable a larger number of employees to access provident fund savings, pension and insurance protection under the applicable EPFO schemes.

This will strengthen retirement savings, pension protection and insurance-linked social security for a larger section of workers.

title: Inaugural PDUNASS–GNLU Executive Program on Labour Law and Social Security Compliance Concludes at Gandhinagar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 SEP 2026 11:56AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The inaugural cohort of the Executive Development Program on Labour Law and Social Security Compliance (EPFO at Core) concluded on 12 September 2026 at Gujarat National Law University (GNLU) with a valedictory and certificate distribution ceremony. Jointly developed by GNLU and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS), the apex training academy of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), the three-month executive programme brought together 60 industry practitioners for rigorous hybrid learning, practical case studies and written assessments.
The programme was conceptualised by Shri Kumar Rohit, Additional Central PF Commissioner (HQ) and Director, PDUNASS, to address the persistent gap between classroom theory and practical enterprise compliance. The initiative seeks to foster a cultural shift in corporate governance from defensive and reactive compliance to informed and ethical compliance.
The vision took institutional shape through sustained collaboration with Prof. (Dr.) S. Shanthakumar, Director, GNLU, whose academic leadership and commitment contributed significantly to establishing a specialised platform for social security education. Dr. Nitin Malik, Registrar, GNLU, provided proactive institutional facilitation and administrative support.
A key feature of the programme was its dynamic and evolving curriculum, designed to respond continuously to statutory reforms, technological advancements and changing workplace environments. During the inaugural cycle, the curriculum was updated in real time to incorporate transition mechanisms under the Code on Social Security 2020, the revised EPF, EPS and EDLI scheme frameworks, and operational practices aligned with live EPFO digital portal workflows.
Launched on May 29, 2026, the programme commenced on June 5 and featured 23 interactive evening sessions led by 16 senior resource persons, including EPFO policymakers and legal academics. The programme culminated in a four-day campus immersion at GNLU from September 9 to 12, featuring practical compliance case studies and formal written evaluations.
The valedictory ceremony was chaired by Chief Guest Dr. Justice K. J. Thakar, Former Judge of the High Courts of Gujarat and Allahabad and Chairperson of the Gujarat State Human Rights Commission. Highlighting the constitutional and human dimensions of social welfare, Justice Thakar observed that provident fund legislation constitutes a foundational safety net for India’s workforce. Drawing upon his extensive judicial experience, he commended the joint institutional initiative and congratulated Shri Kumar Rohit for identifying an important systemic need and translating it into an impactful executive education programme.
Addressing the participants, Shri Kumar Rohit said “This initiative is designed to drive a lasting cultural paradigm shift in enterprise governance transitioning from defensive, checklist compliance to informed, ethical compliance. When compliance is executed with accuracy at the source, returns are clean, administrative friction dissolves, and social security entitlements reach the worker swiftly and with dignity. As the inaugural cohort, you carry the responsibility of being practitioners and ambassadors of this standard across India’s industrial landscape.”
The ceremony was attended by senior officers, including Shri Sudeepta Ghosh, Additional CPFC (Gujarat), and Shri Manoranjan Kumar, RPFC-I, PDUNASS. Dr. Hardik Parikh presented the programme report, outlining its pedagogical outcomes and participant performance.
In view of the strong nationwide response to the inaugural programme, PDUNASS and GNLU announced that admissions for the second batch will open shortly.

title: PM Vishwakarma Completes Three Years: 30 Lakh Artisans Registered Under the Scheme
subtitle:
Third Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma to be Celebrated in Kolkata on 17th September 2026

Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari to Grace the Celebrations
date:

                16 SEP 2026 12:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, will celebrate the Third Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme on 17th September 2026 at the Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal. The event will mark three years of the implementation of the Scheme aimed at providing comprehensive and end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople and strengthening their livelihoods and entrepreneurial capabilities.
Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME, Government of India, along with Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal, will grace the occasion in the august presence of Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State for MSME, Government of India. Shri Dipak Barman, Minister-in-Charge, Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises & Textiles (MSME&T), Government of West Bengal, and Shri Ashok Dinda, Minister of State for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, will also grace the event.
Senior officials from the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, including representatives of the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), and India Post, will also participate in the event.
The event will be attended by PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries, representatives of Gram Panchayats/Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Common Service Centres (CSCs)/Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), and other stakeholders. An exhibition featuring various stalls showcasing products of local artisans and craftspeople will also be organised, providing them with a platform for the display and sale of their products.
Three Years of PM Vishwakarma
The PM Vishwakarma Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 17th September 2023 with the objective of providing end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 identified trades. The Scheme seeks to strengthen the traditional skills of Vishwakarmas by providing them with institutional support, modern tools, access to finance, skill upgradation and market linkages, thereby enabling them to enhance their productivity, income and entrepreneurial potential.
The Scheme provides a comprehensive package of support comprising recognition through PM Vishwakarma certificates and identity cards, skill upgradation, toolkit incentive, credit support, incentives for digital transactions and marketing support.
In a significant milestone achieved within three years of its launch, 30 lakh beneficiaries have been registered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme after completion of the prescribed three-stage verification process, thereby achieving the registration target under the Scheme. The Government of West Bengal decided to onboard the Scheme in May 2026. Already, 3,000 beneficiaries have successfully registered after completing the three-stage verification process. Skill training is currently being imparted to the registered beneficiaries.

The celebrations will also showcase the traditional skills, products and entrepreneurial potential of artisans and craftspeople, providing them a platform to connect with wider markets and opportunities.
The Third Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma marks an important milestone in the Government’s continued efforts to preserve and promote traditional skills, equip artisans with modern tools and knowledge, facilitate access to institutional credit and markets, and enable Vishwakarmas to build sustainable livelihoods and emerge as successful entrepreneurs.
